title: Per-fixture goal rates across the FPL horizon
description: Home and away goal rates for every unfinished fixture in the next `horizon` gameweeks, from the Dixon-Coles posterior and optionally blended toward a no-vig market. Written by pipeline/models/fixture_rates.py::export_fixture_xg and read by load_exported_rates in the same module. The rates set every clean-sheet and goal probability the horizon optimiser ranks on, so shape is the least of it: the invariants that matter are numeric and live in pipeline/fpl/artifacts.py::validate_fixture_xg, which runs before the file is written.

source.description: Payload-level provenance. Says only that AT LEAST ONE fixture was anchored — a consumer must read each row's own `rate_source`, because reading this instead reports every fixture as market-blended the moment one is.

statistical_component.description: Which model was blended with the market. The betting path uses the 60/30/10 ensemble instead; naming it here makes that divergence a claim rather than an accident.

first_gameweek.description: The lowest UNFINISHED gameweek, taken from the event flags. Not necessarily the lowest gameweek present: rows are filtered on per-fixture `finished`, which FPL flips independently, so a week whose matches have all been played can legitimately export nothing.

prior_only_clubs.description: Clubs the posterior has never seen — a promoted side. Their fixtures are served from the league-average prior, and are flagged so nothing downstream mistakes them for evidence-backed.

blend_weight.description: Weight on the market in log-rate space. Zero is a true no-op, including the level correction, so the anchor's contribution can be isolated.

level_correction.description: RAW league-wide log correction, applied at `blend_weight` to EVERY gameweek including unpriced ones. This is what keeps week 1 and week 2 on one scale, and it is the substitute for extrapolating odds. Clamped at ±0.20: beyond that is a data problem, not a discovery.

n_priced.description: Fixtures that reached the inverter, EXCLUDING those with no market for this kickoff — which is the ordinary state for a week the bookmakers have not priced, not a failure.

blend_weight_status.description: Whether market.blend_weight is a bare prior, a prior confirmed out of sample, or a fitted value. Not a boolean: the fit confirmed the prior rather than replacing it.

match_id.description: The FPL fixture id, as a string. Unique within the payload: the consumer keys rates by it, so a duplicate discards one fixture's rates and serves the other's for both.

lambda_home_dc.description: The posterior mean BEFORE any market anchor. Kept so the blend is auditable and reversible from the artifact alone.

prior_only.description: True when either club is outside the posterior's team index, so the rates come from its league-average prior. Such rows are blended at the higher market.prior_only_weight.

lambda_home.description: The rate the consumer uses. Where a market is present this lies between `lambda_home_dc` and `market.lambda_home`, up to the league level correction that every fixture receives regardless of its own market.

rate_source.description: Per-row provenance. `market_blend` requires this row's `market` to be present and converged; the converse holds wherever the blend weight is positive.

supremacy.description: lambda_home - mu_away, at the exported 6-decimal precision.

market.description: The no-vig market-implied rates for this fixture, or null where the bookmakers have not priced it. Present only for a converged, usable inversion.

dispersion.description: Cross-book logit disagreement. Never 0 for a single book — an unmeasurable dispersion is reported as the 0.20 floor, because a consumer dividing by it would otherwise hand one book the maximum weight.

residual.description: UNWEIGHTED logit RMS at the optimum, so it is comparable across fixtures with different book coverage. A large value means a Dixon-Coles bivariate Poisson cannot represent this market at all — usually a stale leg.

weight.description: This market's own quality, from book coverage. It scales only the fixture-specific part of the blend; the league level keeps the full blend weight, because it was estimated from every anchored fixture rather than from this one.
